started on antibiotics. His hospital course was complicated by

shoulder joints. His right shoulder was particularly painful and 

was tapped for fluid, yet not found to have any bacteria, but 
did 
have increased 3+ plus polys. He was treated with 14-day course 
of vancomycin and ceftriaxone that was switched to clindamycin 
on 
___ due to anemia. He now continues on clindamycin. His joint 
involvement partially resolved and now is left with residual 
left 
hip pain and right shoulder pain. The right shoulder pain has 
improved, however, since antibiotics were started. He now 
presents to see us with questions about management of his right 
shoulder pain. He does note decreased function of his right 
shoulder secondary to the pain and stiffness. He has not had any 

therapy for his shoulder. He rates his pain at rest at ___ of 

the right shoulder and ___ with activity. He states that any 
type of movement hurts his right shoulder. He denies any recent 
fevers, chills, redness, swelling about the right shoulder. He 
is on a fentanyl patch as well as oxycodone for the shoulder 
pain.

Discharge Diagnosis:
Right proximal humerus osteomyelitis

 
Discharge Condition:
Stable, NVI.

 
Discharge Instructions:
Activity: Ambulate as tolerated; continue pendulum exercises.  
NWB right arm.

Wound Care: Keep your incisions clean and dry. Do not get your 
incisions wet until after you are seen for your follow-up 
appointment and cleared to do so.  Please place a dry sterile 
dressing to the wound each day if there is drainage, otherwise 
you can leave it open to air. 

Medications:  Please resume your pre-operative medications as 
directed by the prescribing physician(s).  You have been given a 
prescription for a narcotic pain medication.  Stop taking this 
medication as soon as your pain allows. Please take a stool 
softener (such as Colace) if taking narcotic pain medications to 
reduce your symptoms of constipation.   Do not drive, drink 
alcohol or operate machinery while taking narcotic medication.  

Call Dr. ___, your PCP or go to the ER if you 
develop fevers (>101.5)/chills, redness around your incision 
that is warm and tender to the touch, numbness or tingling in 
the hand, increasing pain that doesn't improve with rest and 
pain medication at the prescribed dose, or any other symptoms 
that concern you.

Physical Therapy:
Right shoulder pendulum exercises, NWB right UE.
Treatments Frequency:
PRN dressing changes to right shoulder

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Right shoulder pain, to evaluate humeral head, status post
curettage.

FINDINGS:  In comparison with the study of ___, there is little change
following the curettage.  The area of lucency in the lateral aspect of the
right humeral head is again seen on this post-procedure study.

REASON FOR EXAMINATION:  Evaluation of PICC line placement.

Left PICC line was inserted with its tip terminating in mid SVC.  The
cardiomediastinal silhouette is unchanged and the lungs are clear.  Calcified
left hilar granulomas are again noted, unchanged.
